assessments.reasoning: Section 2.1.6 defines true-valued deactivation with at most one boolean value. Section 3.4 explicitly uses an empty result set for focus-node validation against that deactivated shape.

challenge.method: Compare a true flag, a false or omitted flag, and an ill-formed multiple-value flag. Distinguish the focal shape’s result set from results of other shapes and processor failure in §§3.4.1–3.4.3.
challenge.results: Only a well-formed true flag supplies the stated deactivation branch. Other shapes can still contribute results and ill-formed, recursive or failed validation requires separate handling.

limitations: The empty set applies to the given focus-node and deactivated-shape operation. It does not imply overall conformance or define behavior on invalid input.
